messages:
maya: Heads-up — some prod snapshot restores are failing with KMS AccessDenied. Noticing during a customer restore flow.

tom: which snapshots / tenants? quick logs?

maya: tenant-42, snaps snap-20260320-01 and snap-20260320-02. Error: DecryptFailed AccessDenied on CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cmk-1234abcd

eli: that CMK is the one we rolled into the new key alias last week. I briefly checked IAM — backup-uploader role still references the old alias in an inline policy change that landed this morning (PR #4123).

lina: @tom can you pull CloudTrail KMS:Decrypt and KMS:GenerateDataKey events around 09:00-09:15 UTC? Also check who modified the role.

sec-bot: Audit log: deploy-bot updated role backup-uploader at 2026-03-20T09:04:12Z. Change: removed policy statement allowing kms:Decrypt on cmk-1234abcd. Trigger: infra/iam-cleanup pipeline.

tom: pulling CT now. snippet:
```
2026-03-20T09:05:03Z KMS Decrypt arn:aws:kms:...cmk-1234abcd AccessDenied principal arn:aws:iam::123456:role/backup-uploader
2026-03-20T09:05:05Z STS AssumeRole backup-uploader succeeded
```

dena: so role can assume but no KMS permissions. Did the pipeline intend to narrow scope? @eli was that intended in the iam-cleanup change?

eli: The PR removed broad kms:* on all CMKs and replaced with kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey for service uploads. We missed adding explicit kms:Decrypt for restore path to the backup-service role. Oops.

lina: Confirmed. The backup-uploader is allowed upload path but not decrypt. That explains restores failing. Need temporary mitigations and long-term fix.

oncall-ops: Immediate mitigation: re-add a scoped kms:Decrypt grant for that role to cmk-1234abcd or attach a Customer Managed Policy with least privilege for decrypt on the specific key alias. Which do we prefer for speed?

maya: For speed, reapply a narrow inline allow for kms:Decrypt on the specific key ARN and log the change. Then follow with proper policy MR for vetting.

eli: I'll draft the inline allow and push a hotfix. Proposed statement:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cmk-1234abcd"
}
```

sec-bot: Note — any inline change will create an audit event. Make sure to include reason and link to this thread in the change description.

tom: also recommend rotating the CMK grant model: use KMS grants for short-lived decrypt rights during restore jobs (Grant tokens) instead of persistent wide policies. Grants show up in CloudTrail and can be revoked.

dena: Agree. Grants + strict IAM for upload path. For now, hotfix and a follow-up RFC for grants + role scoping.

lina: Are there any backup artifacts already uploaded encrypted with a different key? We should inventory: run query against snapshot metadata table -> key_id column.

eli: Quick query result: 2 snapshots (the ones failing) reference cmk-1234abcd. Most older ones use cmk-old-2024. No evidence of mass mix.

maya: Customer impact: two restore attempts failed. I'm drafting an incident notification to affected customer and will include ETA once hotfix done.

oncall-ops: Hotfix pushed at 6112233500 -> inline allow reapplied. Can someone validate a restore now?

tom: re-run restore workflow, logs:
```
2026-03-20T09:12:27Z KMS Decrypt cmk-1234abcd Success principal backup-uploader
2026-03-20T09:12:30Z Restore job started --> completed
```

dena: Verified restore succeeded end-to-end. Good.

eli: Next steps (action items):
- eli: open MR to add least-privilege policy and remove inline hotfix (link to MR)
- lina: inventory snapshots with mixed keys and produce a migration plan for tenant-42 if needed
- tom: prototype KMS Grant workflow for restore service (short-lived grants) and measure feasibility
- maya: customer comms + post-incident note
- sec-bot: add automated check in iam-cleanup pipeline to ensure backup restore paths retain kms:Decrypt requirement

maya: I'll create a short postmortem doc and tag eng-sre + product-security. Also logging improvement: add an explicit alert for KMS AccessDenied on restore flows (currently aggregated under generic restore-fails metric).

sec-bot: Alert idea noted: create metric filter on KMS Decrypt AccessDenied events tied to snapshot-restore job IDs.

lina: RFC for long-term: prefer key aliasing policy (backup-service uses alias/backup-default) and central key rotation process; avoid inline policies that diverge.

dena: Important follow-up: run a policy lint across roles that reference CMKs to detect missing decrypt for restore-capable roles.

eli: Will include tests in infra pipelines to simulate restore flow against a staging CMK alias on every PR.

maya: Thanks all. Postmortem draft in 24h, MR for policy in 2h. @sec-bot please keep audit record of these changes. :white_check_mark:
